prompt: Freivalds checks an integer matrix product with exact arithmetic and a fresh random binary vector. If the two resulting vectors disagree, what may you conclude?

options.text: The claimed matrix product is definitely wrong
options.explanation: A correct matrix product agrees for every vector; only agreement can be a false positive.

options.text: The product is wrong with probability only one half
options.explanation: One half bounds the chance a wrong product escapes one trial, not the certainty of a detected mismatch.

options.text: The algorithm must recompute the full product before rejecting
options.explanation: Three matrix–vector products suffice to exhibit a mismatch.

options.text: Floating-point implementations have the same exact guarantee automatically
options.explanation: Rounding changes the arithmetic model and needs separate analysis.

workedExample: A correct product gives the same vector whichever multiplication route is taken. A wrong product can agree on some vectors, but at least half expose a discrepancy under the exact-arithmetic model. Three matrix–vector products avoid recomputing the matrix product. A mismatch is conclusive; repeated agreement is only bounded-error evidence.
